prompt_caching.simple_definition: Storing previously processed prompt text in server memory so the AI doesn't re-read static instructions on every turn.
prompt_caching.eli5: Imagine you order the same coffee every morning. The barista already knows your order, so they don't ask again. They just make it.
prompt_caching.real_life_analogy: Ordering your regular coffee at a cafe. They remember your milk preference instead of asking you to explain it from scratch every single day.
prompt_caching.business_explanation: Reduces API token costs by 50% to 90% on repeated system prompts, saving millions of rupees on recurring enterprise workloads.
prompt_caching.technical_explanation: Calculates cryptographic hashes over prefix token sequences. Matches are loaded directly from GPU KV cache memory, bypassing the Transformer prefill attention phase.
prompt_caching.sarvax_example: SARVAX sends a 20,000-token system prompt containing compliance rules and portfolio guidelines. Prompt caching ensures SARVAX only pays full price once.
prompt_caching.when_to_use: High-volume workflows with identical system prompts, standard document templates, or long conversation histories.
prompt_caching.when_not_to_use: Dynamic, highly changing prompts shorter than 1,024 tokens where cache lookup overhead exceeds prefill time.
advantages: Cuts input token costs by up to 90%
Reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) latency by 2x-4x
limitations: Requires 1,024+ minimum token threshold
5-minute cache TTL expiration on standard endpoints
prompt_caching.cost_impact: Massive Cost Reduction (Reduces input token price from ₹250.50 to ₹25.05 per 1M tokens).

batch_api.simple_definition: Submitting a large queue of requests to be processed asynchronously overnight in exchange for a 50% discount.
batch_api.eli5: Like dropping off your laundry to be washed overnight instead of doing an emergency 1-hour express wash.
batch_api.real_life_analogy: Sending mail via standard economy delivery instead of express overnight courier. It takes a little longer, but costs half the price.
batch_api.business_explanation: Allows enterprises to process bulk reports, background audits, and portfolio analysis at a flat 50% discount on all token costs.
batch_api.technical_explanation: Requests are enqueued in provider worker pools during off-peak GPU utilization windows with a 24-hour non-deterministic SLA.
batch_api.sarvax_example: SARVAX generates 100,000 monthly wealth reports overnight via Batch API, slashing server bills from ₹27.14 Lakhs to ₹2.50 Lakhs.
batch_api.when_to_use: Asynchronous background jobs, cron tasks, weekly portfolio audits, and large-scale data extraction.
batch_api.when_not_to_use: Realtime user interfaces (OneChat) where the user is waiting for an instant response.
advantages: Flat 50% cost reduction across input and output tokens
Higher rate limit ceilings
limitations: Up to 24-hour completion SLA
Not suitable for interactive chat
batch_api.cost_impact: Direct 50% Reduction in Total Infrastructure Expense.

context_window.simple_definition: The maximum amount of text (tokens) an AI model can read and remember in a single interaction.
context_window.eli5: Like how many pages of a book you can keep in your mind at once without forgetting the beginning.
context_window.real_life_analogy: A workbench. A larger workbench lets you spread out 10 full binders side-by-side instead of stacking them.
context_window.business_explanation: Determines whether an AI can ingest a full 100-page bank statement or SEC filing without chopping it into pieces.
context_window.technical_explanation: Maximum sequence length bounded by GPU VRAM allocations for quadratic $O(N^2)$ or linear $O(N)$ attention mechanisms.
context_window.sarvax_example: Gemini 3 Pro's 2,000,000 token context window allows SARVAX to ingest 5 full years of client tax returns and portfolio reports in one prompt.
context_window.when_to_use: Analyzing multi-page contracts, legal discovery, full codebases, and historical financial transcripts.
context_window.when_not_to_use: Short single-question queries where sending huge context inflates latency and token cost unnecessarily.
advantages: Eliminates document chunking errors
Preserves global cross-document context
limitations: Higher memory usage
Needle-in-a-haystack retrieval degradation if context is noisy
context_window.cost_impact: Linear increase in total input tokens billed per request.

graphrag.simple_definition: Retrieval-Augmented Generation that builds an interconnected knowledge graph of entities and relationships rather than matching plain text chunks.
graphrag.eli5: Instead of searching for matching words in a pile of papers, it builds a detective board showing who is connected to whom.
graphrag.real_life_analogy: A company organization chart or family tree showing direct connections between people, roles, and accounts.
graphrag.business_explanation: Prevents AI hallucinations in complex wealth management by understanding how holding companies, trusts, and tax accounts link together.
graphrag.technical_explanation: Combines LLM entity extraction with graph clustering algorithms (Leiden) to generate hierarchical community summaries.
graphrag.sarvax_example: SARVAX uses GraphRAG to map a high-net-worth client's holding companies, trusts, and offshore accounts to recommend tax harvesting.
graphrag.when_to_use: Complex multi-document financial intelligence, corporate due diligence, and risk mapping.
graphrag.when_not_to_use: Simple single-document keyword search where standard vector RAG is faster and cheaper.
advantages: Substantially reduces hallucinations
Discovers multi-hop entity relationships
limitations: Higher upfront index construction cost
Requires graph database storage
graphrag.cost_impact: Slightly higher indexing cost, but dramatically lowers token usage during final reasoning.

mcp.simple_definition: An open standard that connects AI models to external tools, databases, and enterprise software securely.
mcp.eli5: Like a universal USB plug that lets the AI connect to any software in your office.
mcp.real_life_analogy: A universal adapter plug that lets your phone charger fit into wall outlets in any country in the world.
mcp.business_explanation: Allows SARVAX agents to safely read and write to Salesforce, HubSpot, Morningstar, and core banking systems without custom API code.
mcp.technical_explanation: Client-server protocol utilizing JSON-RPC over stdio or HTTP SSE for dynamic tool auto-discovery, prompt templates, and resource access.
mcp.sarvax_example: SARVAX uses an MCP server to fetch live stock prices from Morningstar and automatically update the client's Salesforce CRM record.
mcp.when_to_use: Integrating AI agents with external SaaS platforms, databases, and enterprise APIs.
mcp.when_not_to_use: Isolated offline tasks that require zero external data access.
advantages: Standardized security boundary
Zero custom API integration code required
limitations: Requires running MCP server process
Tool discovery adds minor latency overhead
mcp.cost_impact: Neutral on token costs, but slashes engineering integration hours by 80%.

agent.simple_definition: An autonomous AI software worker that can plan, make decisions, use tools, and execute multi-step business tasks.
agent.eli5: Like a digital assistant that doesn't just answer your questions, but actually goes and does the work for you.
agent.real_life_analogy: A junior financial analyst who receives a task, searches the web, checks company databases, drafts a report, and sends it to you for review.
agent.business_explanation: Shifts AI from passive chatbots ('User operates AI') to autonomous business execution ('AI operates work'), recovering thousands of person-hours.
agent.technical_explanation: Looping state machine combining LLM reasoning, long-term vector memory, tool schema execution (MCP/JSON), and self-correction reflection loops.
agent.sarvax_example: SARVAX deploys an autonomous Due Diligence Agent that crawls news, extracts financial records, checks regulatory compliance, and drafts a report.
agent.when_to_use: Multi-step workflows requiring tool integration, web research, file management, and autonomous decision making.
agent.when_not_to_use: Deterministic, single-step data operations where a fixed code script is faster, cheaper, and 100% predictable.
advantages: Automates complex multi-hour human workflows
Adapts autonomously to unexpected document layouts
limitations: Higher token consumption per task
Requires strict human-in-the-loop audit gates
agent.cost_impact: Consumes 3x-8x more tokens than simple chat, but recovers 90%+ of human operational costs.

structured_outputs.simple_definition: Forcing the AI to format its answer in strict, machine-readable JSON data schemas.
structured_outputs.eli5: Like giving the AI a form with boxes where it MUST fill in each field cleanly without adding extra chatty text.
structured_outputs.real_life_analogy: A tax filing form. Every number must go into its exact designated box, or the tax department rejects the submission.
structured_outputs.business_explanation: Ensures AI outputs can be directly ingested into enterprise CRMs (Salesforce/HubSpot) and core banking software without breaking API integrations.
structured_outputs.technical_explanation: Constrains LLM token generation using context-free grammars (CFG) or JSON Schema token sampling logits masks at the decoder level.
structured_outputs.sarvax_example: SARVAX extracts client passport details and automatically formats them into a strict JSON payload for KYC compliance processing.
structured_outputs.when_to_use: Extracting form data, CRM writeback, database population, and feeding downstream code scripts.
structured_outputs.when_not_to_use: Creative, open-ended research writing where freeform Markdown prose is preferred.
advantages: 100% schema adherence guarantee
Zero JSON parse errors in backend code
limitations: Slightly restricts creative reasoning depth
Requires predefined JSON schema
structured_outputs.cost_impact: Neutral on pricing, but eliminates API integration error recovery costs.

tau_banking.simple_definition: An independent, rigorous benchmark that tests how accurately an AI model performs complex banking and financial advisory tasks.
tau_banking.eli5: A tough exam specifically designed for bank managers and wealth advisors.
tau_banking.real_life_analogy: The Certified Financial Planner (CFP) exam testing a wealth manager's knowledge of tax law, portfolio allocation, and banking rules.
tau_banking.business_explanation: Identifies which AI models can be trusted with actual customer money, tax calculations, and wealth management advice.
tau_banking.technical_explanation: Multi-step tool-use and mathematical evaluation suite measuring accuracy across banking API interactions, ledger balances, and compliance constraints.
tau_banking.sarvax_example: Kimi K3 ranks #1 globally on TAU Banking (0.3340), leading SARVAX to select it as the primary financial reasoning engine.
tau_banking.when_to_use: Evaluating models for wealth management, banking chatbots, tax planning, and credit underwriting.
tau_banking.when_not_to_use: General creative writing or coding tasks where SWE-bench or MMLU-Pro are better indicators.
advantages: Directly measures financial services domain competence
Tests math and tool execution together
limitations: Focused strictly on banking domain
Evolving test set requiring continuous validation
tau_banking.cost_impact: Guides model selection to maximize accuracy per rupee spent.

react_loop.simple_definition: An iterative execution cycle where an AI agent alternates between thinking, executing tool calls, observing outputs, and adjusting its next action.
react_loop.eli5: Imagine a detective solving a puzzle: they think of a clue, look for evidence, read what they found, and then decide what to check next until the mystery is solved.
react_loop.real_life_analogy: A financial advisor reviewing a tax statement: they check income, calculate deductions, look up new tax brackets, and then draft the final tax return.
react_loop.business_explanation: Powers multi-step autonomous AI workers capable of executing complex enterprise workflows without human step-by-step guidance.
react_loop.technical_explanation: Combines step-by-step chain-of-thought prompting with dynamic JSON tool call execution, maintaining an active state history across $N$ execution turns.
react_loop.sarvax_example: SARVAX agents use ReAct loops to fetch client accounts from Salesforce, query Morningstar for stock valuations, and calculate portfolio rebalancing options.
react_loop.when_to_use: Complex multi-step workflows requiring tool interactions, web searches, and dynamic decision trees.
react_loop.when_not_to_use: Simple single-prompt tasks where a direct answer is needed without tool interactions.
advantages: Automates complex multi-step jobs
Adapts dynamically to unexpected API tool errors
limitations: Higher token consumption across turns
Potential for infinite retry loops if un-guarded
react_loop.cost_impact: Multiplies token usage per task by 3x-6x, but slashes human execution hours by 90%.
official_sources: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models (arXiv:2210.03629)

speculative_decoding.simple_definition: Using a tiny, fast drafting model to generate candidate tokens, which a larger model then verifies in a single parallel batch.
speculative_decoding.eli5: A fast assistant writes a quick rough draft, and the senior boss quickly checks and approves 5 words at a time instead of typing letter by letter.
speculative_decoding.real_life_analogy: An intern drafting a routine email signature and opening statement, which the senior partner reviews in 2 seconds.
speculative_decoding.business_explanation: Speeds up large model response time by 2x to 3x without degrading quality or increasing hardware cost.
speculative_decoding.technical_explanation: Speculatively samples $K$ tokens from a lightweight draft model $M_{\text{draft}}$, running a single parallel verification pass on target model $M_{\text{target}}$.
speculative_decoding.sarvax_example: SARVAX uses Gemini Flash as a drafting model for Kimi K3, reducing wealth advisory report generation latency from 12s to 4s.
speculative_decoding.when_to_use: High-latency reasoning models in interactive user chat sessions.
speculative_decoding.when_not_to_use: Batch background jobs where latency is unimportant.
advantages: 2x-3x faster generation speed
Zero impact on output intelligence
limitations: Requires draft model alignment
Higher memory usage
speculative_decoding.cost_impact: Neutral on token price, dramatically reduces TTFT latency.
official_sources: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding (arXiv:2211.17192)

dpo.simple_definition: A technique for aligning AI models with human preferences directly from pairwise choices without training a separate reward model.
dpo.eli5: Like teaching a dog good manners by showing two pictures and pointing to the one with good behavior, instead of giving a complicated score.
dpo.real_life_analogy: A manager reviewing two draft investment memos side-by-side and circling the better structured one.
dpo.business_explanation: Reduces model alignment training costs while improving tone, compliance adherence, and structured JSON formatting accuracy.
dpo.technical_explanation: Implicitly optimizes a classification loss directly over preference pairs $(y_w, y_l)$ using the closed-form solution of the RLHF objective.
dpo.sarvax_example: SARVAX fine-tunes custom wealth advisory agents using DPO on wealth management compliance datasets to prevent illegal financial claims.
dpo.when_to_use: Post-training alignment for tone, enterprise compliance, and output format steering.
dpo.when_not_to_use: Pre-training base models from raw uncurated text documents.
advantages: Simpler & more stable than PPO
Faster alignment iteration cycles
limitations: Requires high-quality preference pair datasets
dpo.cost_impact: Slashes post-training alignment compute costs by 60% compared to PPO RLHF.
official_sources: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model (arXiv:2305.18290)

kv_cache_compression.simple_definition: Techniques to compress the Key-Value memory stored in GPU VRAM during long-context document processing.
kv_cache_compression.eli5: Compressing a long file into a zip folder so it takes up less space in your computer memory while reading.
kv_cache_compression.real_life_analogy: Using shorthand notes during a long lecture instead of writing down every single word verbatim.
kv_cache_compression.business_explanation: Allows self-hosted models (Qwen 3.7 / Llama 4) to serve 4x more concurrent wealth advisor sessions per GPU node, cutting server costs by 75%.
kv_cache_compression.technical_explanation: Quantizes Key and Value matrices to FP8/INT8 and uses GQA (Grouped Query Attention) with page-table memory management.
kv_cache_compression.sarvax_example: SARVAX uses vLLM KV Cache Paging on private AWS A100 clusters to process 50-page PDF financial statements simultaneously.
kv_cache_compression.when_to_use: High-concurrency self-hosted enterprise deployments with long document context requirements.
kv_cache_compression.when_not_to_use: Small single-turn prompt APIs hosted on serverless vendor endpoints.
advantages: 4x higher concurrency capacity per GPU
75% infrastructure cost reduction
limitations: Slight memory quantization overhead
kv_cache_compression.cost_impact: Slashes monthly self-hosted GPU node expenses by up to 75%.
official_sources: vLLM: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving (arXiv:2309.06180)

input_tokens.simple_definition: The atomic sub-word text units sent into an AI model's context window, comprising the system prompt, instructions, background documents, and user queries.
input_tokens.eli5: Think of input tokens like the ingredients in a recipe you read to the chef before they start cooking your meal.
input_tokens.real_life_analogy: Handing a file cabinet full of bank statements and client tax forms to a wealth management paralegal to read before drafting an advisory report.
input_tokens.business_explanation: Input tokens represent 70% to 90% of total LLM payload volume in enterprise workflows; optimizing input token efficiency via prompt caching and chunking directly slashes operational AI expenses.
input_tokens.technical_explanation: Text sequence converted via subword tokenizers (such as Byte-Pair Encoding or Tiktoken) into integer token IDs processed during the Transformer prefill attention phase ($O(N^2)$ or linear attention matrix computations).
input_tokens.sarvax_example: SARVAX ingests a 40-page PDF wealth audit report and tax summary into Gemini 3 Pro as 32,500 input tokens to evaluate portfolio risk.
input_tokens.when_to_use: Structuring system prompts, injecting document context via RAG, passing multi-turn chat history, and defining tool schemas for agents.
input_tokens.when_not_to_use: Passing raw uncompressed repetitive boilerplates when prompt caching or text summarizing could reduce input sequence length.
advantages: Provides the essential context needed for accurate, zero-hallucination reasoning
Priced significantly cheaper per unit than output tokens across all major model providers (typically 3x to 4x cheaper)
limitations: Bounded by the model's maximum context window limit
High input token volume increases prefill latency (Time-to-First-Token) and memory footprint in GPU KV cache
input_tokens.cost_impact: Primary volume driver of LLM costs, but heavily discounted (up to 90%) when leveraging provider prompt caching on static prefix prompts.
official_sources: OpenAI API Documentation on Tokens and Pricing
Anthropic Claude API Reference: Prompt Construction & Tokenization

output_tokens.simple_definition: The generated text units produced autoregressively by an AI model in response to the input prompt.
output_tokens.eli5: Think of output tokens like the actual dish prepared and served by the chef after reading your order.
output_tokens.real_life_analogy: The typed advisory letter and portfolio recommendation report handed back to the client after auditing their financials.
output_tokens.business_explanation: Output tokens are significantly more expensive (3x to 5x higher per token than input tokens) and directly determine total response time and latency for real-time applications.
output_tokens.technical_explanation: Tokens sampled sequentially during the autoregressive decode phase, where each new token requires a GPU forward pass through KV cache memory and softmax probability distribution sampling.
output_tokens.sarvax_example: SARVAX generates a 1,200-output-token personalized portfolio recommendation report in JSON format for a private wealth client.
output_tokens.when_to_use: Generating final executive summaries, structured JSON API responses, code artifacts, and client correspondence.
output_tokens.when_not_to_use: Requesting unnecessarily verbose or conversational padding when concise structured outputs or JSON schemas satisfy the business need.
advantages: Delivers the actual business value, decision, or synthetic artifact requested by the user
Supports fine-grained control via structured JSON mode, max token limits, and stop sequences
limitations: Generates sequentially (one token per step), making output generation the primary bottleneck for system latency
Commanding 3x to 5x higher cost per token compared to input prompt tokens
output_tokens.cost_impact: High Unit Cost (e.g., $15.00/1M output tokens vs $3.00/1M input tokens on frontier models like Claude 3.7 / GPT-4o).

token_consumption.simple_definition: The total aggregate volume of input and output tokens processed by AI models across transactions, agent loops, and system workloads over a given time period.
token_consumption.eli5: Like your monthly electricity bill showing the total kilowatt-hours used by all appliances in your house.
token_consumption.real_life_analogy: Tracking total fuel consumption across a fleet of delivery trucks over a month to calculate operational overhead and mileage efficiency.
token_consumption.business_explanation: The single primary variable metric determining enterprise AI cloud spend; tracking and routing token consumption prevents budget overruns and optimizes cost-per-task ROI.
token_consumption.technical_explanation: Total sum of prefill tokens N_input plus decode tokens N_output measured at provider gateway proxy endpoints or calculated via usage metering headers (usage.prompt_tokens + usage.completion_tokens).
token_consumption.sarvax_example: SARVAX tracks token consumption across 500,000 monthly wealth queries, applying intelligent model routing to keep operational costs under budget.
token_consumption.when_to_use: Capacity planning, FinOps cloud cost monitoring, tier-based billing, and routing optimization across agent workflows.
token_consumption.when_not_to_use: Evaluating single deterministic mathematical calculations where fixed traditional code execution consumes zero tokens.
advantages: Enables precise unit economics calculation down to individual user sessions or agent tasks
Provides measurable telemetry data to drive model routing and prompt optimization
limitations: Varies dynamically based on user input length, multi-turn agent iterations, and unexpected prompt expansions
Requires active observability infrastructure (e.g., OpenTelemetry, Helicone, Langfuse) to monitor effectively
token_consumption.cost_impact: Direct Driver of OpEx Spend; unmonitored agent loops can cause exponential token consumption spikes without rate limiting.
official_sources: Anthropic Enterprise Billing & Cost Management Documentation

embeddings.simple_definition: Dense numerical vector representations of text, images, or audio that capture underlying semantic meaning in a multi-dimensional mathematical space.
embeddings.eli5: Like turning sentences into map coordinates where words with similar meanings (like 'cat' and 'kitten') end up standing right next to each other.
embeddings.real_life_analogy: A library cataloguing system that groups books by topic, era, and reading level rather than just organizing them alphabetically by title.
embeddings.business_explanation: Enables semantic search and RAG across unstructured enterprise data (PDFs, transcripts, filings), allowing employees to find exact information without matching exact keywords.
embeddings.technical_explanation: High-dimensional float vector representations (e.g., 1536-d or 3072-d arrays) generated by specialized encoder Transformer models, compared using cosine similarity or Euclidean distance metrics.
embeddings.sarvax_example: SARVAX converts 100,000 client investment policy statements into 1536-dimensional embeddings stored in Qdrant for semantic search.
embeddings.when_to_use: Semantic document retrieval, vector database indexing, text clustering, duplicate detection, and recommendation systems.
embeddings.when_not_to_use: Exact numerical matching (e.g., looking up exact account number 'ACC-883912') where relational SQL indexing or BM25 keyword search is exact and faster.
advantages: Captures conceptual intent and semantic meaning beyond literal word matches
Generates once, searches millions of times at extremely low compute and token costs
limitations: Cannot guarantee 100% precision for exact strings, proper nouns, or code syntax without hybrid keyword search
Dimensionality and chunk length tradeoffs impact retrieval precision
embeddings.cost_impact: Extremely Cheap (e.g., $0.02 to $0.13 per 1M tokens), making dense vector indexing negligible compared to LLM generation costs.
official_sources: Hugging Face Text Embeddings Inference (TEI) Guide

rag.simple_definition: An architecture that dynamically retrieves relevant facts from external knowledge stores and feeds them into the AI prompt to produce grounded, accurate answers.
rag.eli5: Instead of making a student take an open-book exam purely from memory, you let them look up the exact textbook pages before writing their answers.
rag.real_life_analogy: A financial auditor opening official bank ledger books to verify account balances before writing an audit certification report.
rag.business_explanation: Eliminates AI hallucinations by anchoring model answers to official internal company documents, compliance standards, and real-time market data.
rag.technical_explanation: Two-stage architecture combining dense vector semantic lookup (or hybrid BM25/vector search) to extract top-K document chunks, injected dynamically into the LLM context window during prompt prefill.
rag.sarvax_example: SARVAX uses RAG to retrieve active RBI regulations and client portfolio guidelines, ensuring generated financial advice is 100% compliant.
rag.when_to_use: Answering queries over proprietary, rapidly changing, or high-compliance enterprise knowledge bases without expensive model retraining.
rag.when_not_to_use: Static general-knowledge queries or tasks where all required context fits easily within a prompt or static model training weights.
advantages: Eliminates model hallucinations by grounding outputs in primary enterprise sources
Updates system knowledge instantly by adding/updating files without costly model fine-tuning
limitations: Retrieval precision dependent on document chunking, embedding model choice, and ranker quality
May miss global cross-document relationship context unless augmented with GraphRAG or hybrid search
rag.cost_impact: Drastically lowers overall AI spend by avoiding fine-tuning and keeping prompts targeted compared to sending full multi-megabyte document context every turn.
official_sources: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks (Lewis et al., NeurIPS)

fine_tuning.simple_definition: The process of taking a pre-trained foundation model and further training it on a specific, targeted dataset to adapt its behavior, style, domain knowledge, or output format.
fine_tuning.eli5: Imagine a student who finished general school and knows how to read and write. Fine-tuning is sending them to specialized medical school so they learn exact medical vocabulary and how to write prescription notes.
fine_tuning.real_life_analogy: Custom-tailoring an off-the-rack suit: the base jacket already exists in standard sizes, but fine-tuning alters the sleeves and waist to fit your specific body measurements perfectly.
fine_tuning.business_explanation: Fine-tuning enables enterprises to adapt open-source or proprietary AI models to adhere to custom brand guidelines, strict regulatory compliance templates, and domain-specific terminologies without the immense capital expenditure of training a foundation model from scratch. It dramatically improves consistency and domain alignment while reducing prompt context overhead.
fine_tuning.technical_explanation: Fine-tuning modifies model parameters (weights) via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT like LoRA and QLoRA), or preference alignment (RLHF/DPO/KTO). SFT updates model parameters by computing backpropagation gradient loss on supervised target tokens. PEFT methods inject trainable low-rank decomposition matrices into transformer attention layers (e.g., q, v projection matrices) while freezing base model weights, significantly reducing VRAM requirements and compute overhead.
fine_tuning.sarvax_example: Fine-tuning an open-weights model (e.g., Llama-3.3-70B) on SARVAX historical trade settlement archives and ISDA financial derivative contracts to automatically generate validated, regulatory-compliant trade confirmation JSON objects.
fine_tuning.when_to_use: When requiring consistent structured output formats, adherence to domain-specific jargon/style, offline deployment of lightweight models, latency reduction by removing lengthy prompt instructions, or specialized task alignment.
fine_tuning.when_not_to_use: When domain facts change dynamically and frequently (use RAG instead), when training dataset size is insufficient (< 1,000 high-quality examples), when dynamic prompt engineering achieves target accuracy, or when rapid zero-shot experimentation is required.
advantages: Enforces deterministic adherence to complex response formats and domain-specific output structures.
Reduces prompt token length, lowering per-query inference costs and latency.
Enables smaller specialized models (e.g., 8B-14B) to rival or outperform larger base models on domain tasks.
Provides complete data privacy and control when deployed on private cloud or on-premise infrastructure.
limitations: Risk of catastrophic forgetting, where the model loses baseline general reasoning or general knowledge capabilities.
Requires upfront computational resources, high-quality curated dataset preparation, and ongoing model maintenance.
Static knowledge bottleneck: model weights become outdated as dynamic domain facts evolve.
Potential for over-fitting to training distribution, degrading performance on out-of-distribution inputs.
fine_tuning.cost_impact: Higher upfront capital compute cost for dataset processing and training runs (GPU hours for SFT/PEFT), offset by lower ongoing operational inference costs due to shortened prompt context windows and smaller model footprints.

reasoning_models.simple_definition: AI models specifically trained or architected to perform long step-by-step internal deliberation (Chain-of-Thought) and self-correction prior to emitting a final response, excelling at math, code, logic, and multi-step reasoning.
reasoning_models.eli5: Instead of blurting out the first answer that pops into its head like standard AI, a reasoning model stops, scratches its chin, writes down step-by-step notes in its head, double-checks its work for mistakes, and then gives you the final correct answer.
reasoning_models.real_life_analogy: A master chess grandmaster who spends several minutes deliberating, testing potential variations, and evaluating moves on a mental scratchpad before physically making a move on the board.
reasoning_models.business_explanation: Reasoning models transform high-stakes enterprise decision-making by replacing simple probabilistic text completion with rigorous inference-time search and validation. They significantly reduce hallucinations in complex domain analysis such as legal contract auditing, complex tax modeling, financial derivative risk evaluation, and advanced software architecture debugging.
reasoning_models.technical_explanation: Reasoning models leverage inference-time compute scaling (Test-Time Compute) alongside Reinforcement Learning (RL) trained on process-based reward models (PRMs) or self-play CoT search algorithms (e.g., Monte Carlo Tree Search, Search-over-Thoughts). During inference, the model generates explicit internal thinking tokens (hidden or visible Chain-of-Thought) to evaluate hypotheses, backtrack on errors, and refine reasoning before producing final user tokens.
reasoning_models.sarvax_example: Deploying OpenAI o1/o3 or DeepSeek R1 to analyze multi-jurisdictional Basel III capital adequacy calculations for SARVAX banking clients, verifying intermediate math formulas and regulatory logic chains before issuing audit statements.
reasoning_models.when_to_use: For multi-step mathematical computation, formal logic verification, complex software bug analysis, multi-layered legal or tax analysis, and tasks where accuracy is paramount and higher latency/cost is acceptable.
reasoning_models.when_not_to_use: For simple conversational chat, basic summary generation, high-throughput real-time voice applications, low-latency streaming tasks, or simple retrieval lookup where standard foundation models suffice.
advantages: Substantially higher accuracy and dramatic reduction in factual and logical hallucinations on complex tasks.
Inherent self-correction capabilities: capable of identifying and amending mistakes within its internal thought loop.
Extends capabilities on challenging STEM, algorithmic coding, and formal quantitative analysis.
Scales performance dynamically with increased test-time compute allocation.
limitations: Higher time-to-first-token (TTFT) and increased overall latency due to extensive chain-of-thought token generation.
Increased cost per query stemming from consuming large numbers of internal reasoning tokens.
May over-think simple straightforward queries, generating unnecessary computational overhead.
Hidden internal reasoning tokens (in proprietary models) reduce direct visibility into exact step-by-step telemetry.
reasoning_models.cost_impact: Substantially higher inference costs per request due to generating hundreds or thousands of internal reasoning tokens before final output generation, requiring balanced routing strategies.
related_concepts: DeepSeek R1 / OpenAI o1 / OpenAI o3

agentic_ai.simple_definition: AI systems capable of autonomously perceiving their environment, setting intermediate goals, executing multi-step task plans using external tools and APIs, and adapting actions based on environment feedback without requiring step-by-step human intervention.
agentic_ai.eli5: Instead of just answering your question like a dictionary, an Agentic AI acts like a smart personal assistant who takes your high-level goal, breaks it down into a task list, uses Google, opens files, runs code, fixes errors on its own, and finishes the whole job for you.
agentic_ai.real_life_analogy: An autonomous general contractor who receives a high-level goal ('remodel the kitchen'), creates blueprints, purchases materials, coordinates subcontractors, inspects the work, fixes errors, and delivers a completed room.
agentic_ai.business_explanation: Agentic AI shifts enterprise AI from passive content generation to active operational execution. By orchestrating complex workflows across CRM, ERP, code repositories, and external APIs, agentic systems automate end-to-end business operations, dramatically increasing productivity and enabling complex multi-step digital worker workflows.
agentic_ai.technical_explanation: Agentic AI architectures integrate foundation models as central decision-making engines (planners) operating within iterative execution loops (e.g., ReAct: Reason-Act-Observe). They utilize memory modules (short-term context, long-term vector/graph stores), dynamic tool invocation capabilities (function calling, REST APIs, CLI execution, browser automation), subagent delegation, and reflection loops to monitor state changes and self-correct trajectory.
agentic_ai.sarvax_example: An autonomous SARVAX Liquidity Risk Management Agent that monitors market data feeds, detects anomalous volatility, queries collateral databases via SQL, runs Monte Carlo VaR simulations in Python, and drafts structured compliance filings.
agentic_ai.when_to_use: For end-to-end multi-step workflow automation, dynamic tasks requiring tool integration (web browsing, code execution, database queries), non-deterministic environments, and complex multi-system integration.
agentic_ai.when_not_to_use: For simple single-turn query answering, static document formatting, scenarios requiring strict millisecond-level deterministic execution without loop overhead, or safety-critical actions lacking human-in-the-loop review.
advantages: Autonomous execution of multi-step, end-to-end tasks with minimal human intervention.
Dynamic adaptability: capable of switching tools, revising plans, and recovering from runtime errors.
Seamless integration with enterprise infrastructure via function calling, APIs, and CLI tools.
Scalable multi-agent collaboration for complex distributed problem solving.
limitations: Risk of infinite execution loops or compounding error cascade if plan evaluation or tool feedback fails.
Higher token consumption and cumulative latency due to iterative perception-action cycles.
Security risks around tool execution (e.g., unintended API mutations, prompt injection vulnerabilities).
Nondeterministic execution paths make strict auditing and deterministic debugging challenging.
agentic_ai.cost_impact: Variable and potentially high operational costs per task execution due to multi-turn model invocation, repeated tool calling overhead, and long conversation history accumulation.

tool_calling.simple_definition: An AI model capability that enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to interact with external software tools, APIs, databases, and executable code to perform real-world actions or retrieve live data beyond their training cutoff.
tool_calling.eli5: Instead of just answering with what it remembers, the AI can reach out and use tools like a web browser, calculator, or database to get up-to-the-minute answers or do actual tasks for you.
tool_calling.real_life_analogy: A smart assistant who doesn't just give you driving directions from memory, but opens a live GPS app on their smartphone to check current traffic jams before guiding you.
tool_calling.business_explanation: Tool Calling transforms LLMs from passive conversational text generators into actionable autonomous agents. It enables enterprise software to automate workflows, retrieve real-time enterprise data from internal systems (CRM, ERP), execute transactions, and reduce manual human operational overhead while enforcing strict RBAC and compliance controls.
tool_calling.technical_explanation: The LLM client supplies a list of available tools specified as JSON schemas (defining tool names, descriptions, and parameter types/constraints). During inference, when the LLM determines an external operation is required, it halts text generation and emits a structured payload (often tool_calls with call_id, function.name, and JSON-encoded arguments). The host runtime intercepts this request, executes the target local or remote tool via API, and injects the returned tool payload back into the context history as a tool role message for final LLM synthesis.
tool_calling.sarvax_example: In SARVAX, an AI Wealth Advisor agent uses Tool Calling to invoke get_portfolio_valuation(client_id='C1048') and query_market_feed(ticker='AAPL') to compute a client's real-time net worth and tax-loss harvesting recommendations.
tool_calling.when_to_use: Use when an AI application requires live external data lookup, structured multi-step API execution, deterministic computations (e.g. financial math), or interaction with third-party software systems.
tool_calling.when_not_to_use: Do not use for static content generation, general creative writing, simple text summarization, or tasks where latency overhead and external system access are unnecessary or risky.
advantages: Extends model knowledge to real-time, dynamic enterprise systems.
Replaces stochastic model hallucinations with deterministic, verified API outputs.
Enables autonomous multi-agent task execution and complex workflow orchestration.
Enforces typed schema constraints on parameters generated by the LLM.
limitations: Increases overall request latency due to intermediate model turns and API execution round-trips.
Potential risk of indirect prompt injection or unintended system execution if inputs aren't sanitized.
Requires robust error handling when external tools fail or return malformed outputs.
tool_calling.cost_impact: Increases token cost due to passing tool definition schemas on every request and adding multi-turn context history (tool call payload + tool response payload). Infrastructure costs also scale with external API consumption.

function_calling.simple_definition: A targeted subset of tool calling where an LLM structures its output as a formal JSON payload corresponding to a specific programming function signature, allowing host applications to invoke code deterministically.
function_calling.eli5: The AI fills out a structured form with exact values so a computer program can run a specific job without guessing what the AI meant.
function_calling.real_life_analogy: Filling out a bank deposit slip with exact field boxes for account number, cash amount, and date, which the bank teller machine can read automatically without error.
function_calling.business_explanation: Function Calling provides a bridge between unstructured natural language queries and structured enterprise databases/APIs. It enables businesses to convert vague customer requests into precise programmatic API calls, automating back-office transactions, booking services, and database queries with zero syntax ambiguity.
function_calling.technical_explanation: Function Calling relies on fine-tuned model weights trained to strictly output syntactically valid JSON matching predefined JSON Schema representations (parameters, properties, required fields). The host sends the schema under the API parameter (e.g., functions or tools), and the LLM constrains its output decoding to emit valid JSON arguments matching the target signature instead of unstructured conversational text.
function_calling.sarvax_example: A SARVAX compliance agent converts natural language client instructions into a structured submit_rebalance_order(account_id='A882', target_allocation={'equity': 0.60, 'fixed_income': 0.40}) function call payload for core banking processing.
function_calling.when_to_use: Use when converting natural language into structured JSON payloads, executing database queries (e.g., SQL generation), or invoking deterministic code functions within a software platform.
function_calling.when_not_to_use: Do not use when flexible, open-ended conversational responses are required, or when no backend programmatic function exists to consume the output.
advantages: Guarantees structured, machine-readable JSON output parsing.
Reduces parsing failures compared to regex-based or string-scraping LLM extraction.
Enforces parameter type safety and required field validation at the schema layer.
limitations: Model may still hallucinate invalid parameter values or pass out-of-range arguments if schema constraints are ambiguous.
Slightly inflates prompt context size by requiring parameter definitions in every prompt call.
Requires strict client-side validation before executing functions in production.
function_calling.cost_impact: Slightly increases prompt token overhead due to function signature schemas. Reduces retries and parsing errors, lowering total operational token waste.

streaming.simple_definition: A technique in generative AI where response tokens are sent incrementally to the client in real time as they are generated, rather than waiting for the complete response to finish.
streaming.eli5: Watching a movie in real time as it plays, rather than downloading the entire full-length file before you can watch the first second.
streaming.real_life_analogy: A waiter bringing out appetizers as soon as they are cooked, rather than making you sit hungry until all 10 party entrees are completely ready.
streaming.business_explanation: Streaming radically improves perceived performance and User Experience (UX) in AI applications. By displaying initial tokens within milliseconds (low Time To First Token / TTFT), enterprise platforms reduce user drop-off, increase engagement, and provide immediate visual feedback during long text generation tasks.
streaming.technical_explanation: Streaming utilizes HTTP Server-Sent Events (SSE) or WebSockets to transmit token chunks over a persistent HTTP connection (Transfer-Encoding: chunked). As the autoregressive LLM decoder samples each token (or small chunk of tokens), the server formats it into an SSE event (data: {"choices": [{"delta": {"content": "..."}}]}) and flushes the buffer to the network socket immediately.
streaming.sarvax_example: In the SARVAX Executive Portal, financial summary reports stream token-by-token directly to the user dashboard using Server-Sent Events (SSE), enabling instant reading while back-end analytical charts finish rendering.
streaming.when_to_use: Use for interactive user interfaces, conversational chatbots, long-form document generation, and real-time status reporting where low perceived latency is critical.
streaming.when_not_to_use: Do not use for background batch processing, automated backend-to-backend integrations, structured JSON generation where full validation is required before processing, or offline analytical jobs.
advantages: Dramatically lowers Time To First Token (TTFT) and perceived user latency.
Provides instant feedback and interactive engagement for long responses.
Allows clients to cancel generation mid-stream if the response is off-target, saving tokens.
limitations: Requires maintaining persistent HTTP connections (SSE/WebSockets), placing higher memory demands on API gateways.
Complicates structured data validation (JSON parsing) until the full stream completes.
Handling stream interruptions and network drops requires complex client-side reconnection logic.
streaming.cost_impact: Does not alter token pricing directly, but reduces server memory footprint per request duration by streaming chunks. Can reduce costs if users cancel unwanted long generations early.

latency.simple_definition: The time delay between sending a request to an AI system and receiving a response, typically measured in milliseconds or seconds.
latency.eli5: The time you wait from when you ask a question to when the person starts speaking their answer.
latency.real_life_analogy: The delay between pressing the gas pedal in a car and feeling the vehicle accelerate forward.
latency.business_explanation: Latency directly dictates user satisfaction, application usability, and system SLA compliance. High latency in AI systems leads to user frustration and churn, whereas low latency unlocks real-time voice assistants, high-frequency financial trading analytics, and seamless interactive workflows.
latency.technical_explanation: In LLM systems, total latency consists of two main components: Time To First Token (TTFT) and Time Per Output Token (TPOT). TTFT measures prefill phase latency (prompt token ingestion, KV-cache loading, context computation overhead), while TPOT measures autoregressive decoding phase latency per generated token. Total Latency = TTFT + (TPOT * Total Output Tokens) + Network Round-Trip Time (RTT).
latency.sarvax_example: The SARVAX high-frequency wealth query service targets a TTFT SLA under 250ms and total generation latency under 1.5 seconds for instant investment advisory responses.
latency.when_to_use: Latency is a critical engineering performance metric evaluated continuously across API endpoint selection, model sizing (SLM vs LLM), caching strategies, and infrastructure deployment.
latency.when_not_to_use: Do not optimize latency at the total expense of output quality or reasoning accuracy for complex analytical, financial, or legal reasoning tasks.
advantages: Low latency enables smooth real-time interactive user experiences and conversational agents.
Improves overall platform throughput and system utilization efficiency.
Reduces timeout errors in multi-tiered enterprise architecture integrations.
limitations: Low-latency models (smaller SLMs or quantized models) may trade off reasoning depth and task accuracy.
Low-latency infrastructure (H100/B200 GPUs, speculative decoding, KV caching) carries higher hardware costs.
latency.cost_impact: Reducing latency often requires premium hardware hosting (e.g. specialized GPUs, high-bandwidth memory), spec-decoding, or dedicated provisioned throughput, which increases operational expenditure.

throughput.simple_definition: The volume of work processed by an AI system within a given timeframe, commonly measured in Tokens Per Second (TPS) or Requests Per Minute (RPM).
throughput.eli5: How many customers a fast-food counter can serve in one single hour.
throughput.real_life_analogy: The number of gallons of water flowing through a main pipe every minute.
throughput.business_explanation: Throughput defines the operational capacity and scalability of an enterprise AI infrastructure. High throughput allows a business to support thousands of concurrent enterprise users, process massive batch document archives, and minimize cost per request through optimal GPU batching.
throughput.technical_explanation: LLM inference throughput is measured at both system level (total output tokens generated across all concurrent sessions per second, e.g. System TPS) and user level (Tokens Per Second delivered to an individual user stream). Modern inference engines (e.g., vLLM, TGI, TensorRT-LLM) maximize throughput using continuous batching (iteration-level batching), PagedAttention (memory-efficient KV cache management), and tensor parallelism across GPU clusters.
throughput.sarvax_example: The SARVAX batch document ingestion engine scales throughput to 15,000 Tokens Per Second across GPU clusters to index 50,000 wealth management PDF reports overnight.
throughput.when_to_use: Use throughput as the key metric when sizing GPU clusters, evaluating enterprise API tier limits, conducting load testing, and optimizing batch background jobs.
throughput.when_not_to_use: Do not focus purely on aggregate system throughput if doing so severely compromises per-user latency (TTFT) in real-time interactive user applications.
advantages: Maximizes hardware resource utilization (GPU Compute & HBM bandwidth).
Lowers per-token operational inference costs through high concurrency and dynamic batching.
Enables large-scale batch processing and multi-tenant enterprise scalability.
limitations: High-throughput continuous batching can cause queue delays, increasing individual user latency under heavy load.
Requires complex memory management (PagedAttention) to prevent GPU VRAM out-of-memory (OOM) crashes.
throughput.cost_impact: Maximizing throughput lowers unit economics (cost per million tokens processed) by driving higher hardware efficiency and amortizing fixed compute infrastructure costs.
